question: The mean and the mode of a set of data are 86.7 and 51.3, respectively. Find the median of the data, using the empirical formula.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The empirical formula is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

⇒ Median = (Mode + 2 × Mean) ÷ 3

⇒ Median = (51.3 + 2 × 86.7) ÷ 3

⇒ Median = (51.3 + 173.4) ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 224.7 ÷ 3 = 74.9

**∴ The correct answer is 74.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = 86.7

Mode = 51.3

**Formula Used:**

Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median)

This empirical rule implies that the Median divides the distance between Mode and Mean in a 2:1 ratio.

 Total Difference = 3 Parts = 86.7 − 51.3 = 35.4

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Difference = Mean − Mode = 86.7 − 51.3 = 35.4

⇒ By the empirical division, 3 Parts = 35.4

⇒ 1 Part = 35.4 ÷ 3 = 11.8

⇒ The Median is located exactly 1 Part away from the Mean.

⇒ Median = Mean − 1 Part

⇒ Median = 86.7 − 11.8 = 74.9

**∴ The correct answer is 74.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical formula established by Karl Pearson is: Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median).

Positively Skewed Distribution

When the distribution tail is stretched to the right side, the measures fall in the order: Mean > Median > Mode.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

When the distribution tail is stretched to the left side, the measures fall in the order: Mean < Median < Mode.

Symmetrical Distribution

For a perfectly normal (bell-shaped) distribution curve, all three central tendencies coincide perfectly: Mean = Median = Mode.
